name: TX-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: Republican-leaning district (R+11 PVI) with incumbent Jake Ellzey renominated
Overwhelming fundraising gap: Ellzey has $2.5M on hand vs. Minton's $14K
Prediction markets price Ellzey around 95% to win
model.rationale: Ellzey combines incumbency, a Republican-leaning seat, and a massive financial advantage against a little-funded challenger, and markets agree the race is effectively decided. With no polls to refine the estimate, the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin with wide uncertainty.
model.watch: Any late independent spending or polling showing Minton gaining traction would be the first sign the race is competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican Jake Ellzey seeks reelection in a North Texas district that leans about eleven points Republican at the presidential level. He was renominated without difficulty and enters the general election with roughly $2.5 million in cash after raising more than $4.6 million this cycle. Democrat Danny Minton has raised about $44,000, leaving him with little money to introduce himself to voters.

No public general-election polls cover the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets put Ellzey's chances around 95 percent. The fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican win in the mid-teens, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any evidence of a genuine contest.
